HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2001 girls soccer archive is thin but gives a clear record path late in the season. Hilton Head Prep defeated St. Andrew's 4-0 in the first recovered full result, with Klie White credited with 20 saves as the Saints fell to 0-4.
Beaufort Academy beat St. Andrew's 5-0 on April 24. Klie White made 13 saves and LeighAnne Evans made 11 as the published line moved St. Andrew's to 0-6.
St. Andrew's broke through against Jefferson Davis Academy on May 2. Meghan Lowe, Sarah Roddenberry, and Ann Cole scored, Klie White made four saves, and the Saints improved to 1-8.

Meghan Lowe, Sarah Roddenberry, and Ann Cole scored in the Jefferson Davis win.

HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2002 girls soccer archive currently has two recovered scored games. St. Andrew's beat Jefferson Davis Academy 4-0 behind goals from LeighAnne Evans, Layne Haggberg, Grace Wilkowski, and Alicia Underwood, improving to 3-7.

The broad OCR sweep surfaced the season-ending Beaufort Academy result inside a St. Vincent's Academy article. Beaufort Academy beat St. Andrew's 2-1 on penalty kicks, with Meghan Lowe scoring and Klie White making 19 saves, including eight on penalty kicks.
Because the Jefferson Davis result listed St. Andrew's at 3-7, the schedule includes two win and seven loss placeholders before April 29 until the missing early-season scores are recovered.

SeasonResult: St. Andrew's reached the SCISA Class AA state semifinals and finished 5-6.
StatusNote: NewsBank confirms St. Andrew's final 5-6 record and state semifinal finish. One state tournament win is inferred from the record path from 4-5 after the regular season to 5-6 after the Lowcountry Day semifinal loss, but the opponent and score are still unrecovered.
HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2003 girls soccer season now has a recovered NewsBank schedule arc under head coach Mark Gibbons. St. Andrew's opened the available record with a 1-0 win over King's Academy, as Meghan Lowe scored from a Maggie Hinchey assist and LeighAnne Evans made six saves.

The Saints built to 3-2 by early April with a 4-1 win over Trinity Collegiate and a 6-2 win over King's Academy. Meghan Lowe scored twice against Trinity and recorded a hat trick in the second King's Academy match, while Grace Wilkowski, Layne Haggberg, Kristen Albritton, and Larkin Butler also appeared in the scoring summaries.

The late regular-season stretch put St. Andrew's in the middle of the region race. Beaufort Academy and Hilton Head Prep handed the Saints back-to-back losses, but St. Andrew's answered with a 1-0 win over Trinity Collegiate before falling 2-0 to Lowcountry Day in the game that decided the region's top two seeds.

St. Andrew's entered the SCISA Class AA state tournament as the Region 1 No. 3 seed. The final published record line shows the Saints won one state tournament match before falling 3-0 to Lowcountry Day in the state semifinals at Pawleys Island to finish 5-6.
HighlightNotes: Finished 5-6 and reached the SCISA Class AA state semifinals.
Meghan Lowe scored at least seven goals in the recovered results, including a hat trick against King's Academy.
LeighAnne Evans and Emily Aimone both appeared in goal in the recovered box scores.
Rebecca Cooper, LeighAnne Evans, Meghan Lowe, and Grace Wilkowski were listed among Hollis Stacy Award candidates in May 2003.

SeasonResult: St. Andrew's followed a third-place finish in the 16-team Cavalier Classic with two wins in the Kelme Tournament of Champions, four recovered region wins, an April 29 win over Beaufort Academy that clinched the SCISA Region 1-AA championship, and a run to the SCISA Class A/AA state final.
StatusNote: Archive build in progress. The May 15 state final report listed St. Andrew's at 14-3 after Greenwood Christian won the championship on penalty kicks. The recovered game list does not yet account for every result in that published record.
HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2004 girls soccer archive currently begins with a March 9 match against Frederica Academy and a March 11 region match against Colleton Prep. Frederica won the opener 4-0, then St. Andrew's answered with a 9-0 SCISA 2-AA region win over Colleton Prep.

St. Andrew's then posted consecutive shutouts at the Cavalier Classic at Mount De Sales High School in Macon, beating Dominion Christian 2-0 and First Presbyterian Day 1-0. Jennifer Moesch scored all three Cavalier Classic goals listed in the March 20 report, and Mary Wilkowski made 13 saves across the two wins.

On March 20, St. Andrew's lost 5-0 to Frederica Academy in the Cavalier Classic semifinal, then defeated Fellowship Christian 3-2 in the third-place game. The Lions placed third out of 16 teams, and Jennifer Moesch and Mary Wilkowski were named to the all-tournament team.

St. Andrew's added two March 27 wins in the Kelme Tournament of Champions, defeating The King's Academy 6-0 and Trinity Collegiate 4-1. Jennifer Moesch scored five goals across the two games, while Mary Wilkowski made five saves.

On March 29, St. Andrew's defeated Beaufort Academy 5-0 in SCISA Region 2-AA play. Jennifer Moesch scored three goals, Leighanne Evans scored twice, and Mary Wilkowski made two saves as the Lions improved to 7-2 overall and 2-0 in the region.

St. Andrew's defeated Colleton Prep 5-1 in an April 1 GISA Region 2-AA game. Layne Haggberg scored twice, and Leighanne Evans, Jennifer Moesch, and Rebecca Timms each scored once as St. Andrew's moved to 8-2 overall and 3-0 in region play.

On April 2, St. Andrew's beat Trinity Collegiate 5-1 in a non-region match. Jennifer Moesch scored three goals, Megan Johnson and Grace Wilkowski also scored, and Rebecca Timms, Emily Aimone, and Moesch recorded assists.
On April 6, St. Andrew's played Hilton Head Christian to a 0-0 draw. Mary Wilkowski made 12 saves as St. Andrew's moved to 9-2-1.

On April 29, St. Andrew's defeated Beaufort Academy 5-0. Jennifer Moesch scored three goals, Grace Wilkowski and Becca Timms also scored, and Emily Aimone recorded an assist as St. Andrew's clinched the SCISA Region 1-AA championship.

In the SCISA Class AA/A state tournament, St. Andrew's defeated The King's Academy 8-0 in the quarterfinals and Lowcountry Day School 5-0 in the semifinals to earn a spot in the state championship at Heathwood Hall School.

St. Andrew's finished as the SCISA Class A/AA State Runner-up after Greenwood Christian beat the Saints 2-1 on penalty kicks in the May 15 state final. Jennifer Moesch scored the tying goal with 2:32 left in regulation, and Mary Wilkowski made 10 saves.

SeasonResult: St. Andrew's finished 4-6, took the No. 3 seed from SCISA Region 1-AA, and lost to Trinity Collegiate in the SCISA Class AA first round.
StatusNote: Archive build in progress. The season now includes 10 recovered results from Apr. 5-May 10, 2005. A May 8 record line appears inconsistent with the surrounding schedule, so the final record follows the May 12 state-tournament report listing St. Andrew's at 4-6.
HistoricalSummary: St. Andrew's opened the recovered Spring 2005 girls soccer schedule with a 3-2 win over Colleton Prep. Becca Timms, Maggie Sammons, and Emily Dunn scored, and Mary Wilkowski made seven saves.
The Saints also beat Pinewood Prep and James Island Christian by 2-1 scores before losing 2-1 to Beaufort Academy despite a Timms goal and 21 saves from Wilkowski.

After losses to Pinewood Prep, Hilton Head Prep, and Beaufort Academy, St. Andrew's beat Colleton Prep 3-1 on April 28. Ann Cole, Emily Dunn, and Becca Timms scored, Clara Rucker assisted all three goals, and Wilkowski made 10 saves.

St. Andrew's was listed as the No. 3 seed from SCISA Region 1-AA after a May 6 loss to James Island Christian. The Saints then lost 2-0 at Trinity Collegiate in the SCISA Class AA first round and finished 4-6.
HighlightNotes: Becca Timms scored in wins over Colleton Prep and Colleton Prep again, and assisted Emily Dunn's goal against Pinewood Prep.
Clara Rucker assisted all three St. Andrew's goals in the April 28 win over Colleton Prep.
Mary Wilkowski made 70 saves across seven recovered box scores.
